/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 04 June 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3037 (-87)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5040 (-213)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2254 (-36)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1584 (1)
Baltic Handysize Index: 862 (7)
CAPESIZE
With Posidonia drawing to a close, there was a slight uptick in activity across the market, though sentiment remained mixed. The Pacific came under renewed pressure, while South Brazil and West Africa to China saw a modest lift in enquiry, albeit with a softer undertone overall. The BCI 182 5TC declined by $1,934 on the day to $45,707, reflecting the weaker tone. In the Pacific, C5 eased $0.735 to $14.535, while C3 slipped $0.218 to $36.632. Pacific sentiment remained softer, with C5 volumes thinner compared to recent weeks. Despite the presence of two miners in the market, support was limited and failed to prevent rates trending lower. Last done on C5 at $15.05 set a weaker tone from the outset, with bids quickly adjusting down to $14.00 following fixtures reported at $14.60 and $14.50, and further operator fixing seen in the $14.25–$14.30 range. In the Atlantic, there was a slight uptick in activity from South Brazil and West Africa to China, with a number of offers seen in the $37.00–$37.50 range, although bid levels remained closer to $36.50. Overall sentiment was a touch softer despite the marginal increase in enquiry.
PANAMAX
The sector experienced another negative day, with sentiment remaining generally weak across both Atlantic and Asian markets. Trans-Atlantic continued to hold a broadly steady tone, with marginally improved bids still largely confined to prompt dates where tonnage remains scarce. On the other hand, the sentiment softened slightly for EC South America, with rates came under increased pressure, particularly for 2H June. Owners were seen revising offers lower, while earlier arrivals showed a greater willingness to accept waiting days. In the Pacific, further losses were observed as we moved towards the end of the trading week, and it feels as though a stronger finish or a decent replenishment of cargoes is needed to steady the market. The AE Jupiter (74,475 2007) Beihai 7 June heard fixed on voyage terms from Indonesia to S China but further details were not disclosed. All these reflected on index and the BPI time charter average fell by $322 to $20,285.
SUPRAMAX
With the events still carrying on in Athens, yet again a rather muted day. Although that said sentiment in most areas remained the same. The US Gulf some felt had eased a little whilst others felt a ceiling had yet to be reached. The South Atlantic remained relatively active, but again fixing information was kept under the radar. The Mediterranean/Continent remained flat and fundamentals changed little. From Asia, further green shoots appeared as positive sentiment gained a foot hold. There was a bit more enquiry both north and south helping owners’ expectations. Period activity surfaced, the Savitree Naree (63,016 2016) open Fos spot was heard to have fixed for short period at $20,500 and redelivery Far East to Centurion. The 11TC average gained $14.00 to stay relatively flat at $20,020.

Atlantic
The Georgios P (57,051 2010) open Port Said was heard to have fixed a trip with clinker to Conakry at $8,250 with Pacific Basin.

Asia
The GW Challenger (61,470 2012) open Sri Lanka 5 June and giving eta Singapore 10 June was heard to have fixed an Indonesia ruin to China with coal $18,250 with Tongli but no more details came to light.

HANDYSIZE
It was a mixed day of activity, with only minor fluctuations observed across both basins. The BHSI rose by 7 points to 862, while the 7TC average increased by $118 to close at $15,508. In the Continent and Mediterranean, activity remained subdued and sentiment largely positional, with rates holding in line with previous fixtures. The U.S. Gulf, however, saw fresh demand and increased activity, with rates reflecting a slightly firmer tone. In contrast, the South Atlantic continued to lag, as ample tonnage and limited fresh demand kept downward pressure on rates. Across Asia, the market remained well supported, with a few more fixtures reported and rates trending upwards. The Julietta D (37,202 2013), open Singapore, was fixed for multiple legs at $17,250 by Oldendorff. In addition, a 38,000 open in the Far East was heard fixed for steels via South Korea to West Coast Mexico at below $18,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Ports Face Mounting Coal Import Congestion

Southern Chinese coal import terminals are facing mounting congestion as strong seaborne arrivals push inventories toward storage limits, tightening discharge capacity across key ports, McCloskey reports. Several port operators said cargo owners are increasingly being required to demonstrate that incoming shipments have been secured by power generators before discharge approvals are granted. Stocks at major hubs including Xinsha, Fangcheng, Putian and Meizhouwan have risen sharply, with vessel waiting times extending to as much as 15 days. The inventory build is being driven by utilities securing fuel ahead of a potentially hotter summer, supportive regional power prices and increased import procurement following recent supply disruptions linked to safety inspections in Shanxi. According to McCloskey, market participants increasingly view current stockpiles as a strategic buffer against domestic supply risks.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The front-end of the Cape FFA curve was under significant pressure today as the physical market continues to slide, while the contracts further down remained relatively stable. The Jun lost the most value with 39000 sold, followed by the July with 32250 trading. The Jun v Jul spread widened and strengthened up to 7000, while the Jul v Aug narrowed and weekend back down to 1500. The Aug v Sep roll was sold down to -1000. Q3 was trading actively within a range of 31500-31800, whereas interest on the Q4 was sporadic and rangebound trading between 31100 and 31200. The Cal27 traded marginally weaker down to 26400 while the Cal28 traded sideways at 22950.

PMX
PMX market was mixed through the session with activity concentrated in the front months and Q3. Jun was again the main focus, trading heavily between 20,600 and 20,800. ai_analysis.summary: 2026年6月4日波罗的海干散货指数全线走弱，BDI下跌87点至3037，Capesize与Panamax领跌。Pacific市场压力加大，C5航线跌破$14.50；Supramax与Handysize逆势小涨，亚洲区域需求初现回暖迹象。FFA曲线呈近弱远强格局，Q3后合约跌幅收窄，市场预期逐步企稳。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: Capesize与Panamax主导下行通道，BCI单日下跌$1,934至$45,707，BPI跌$322至$20,285。Supramax 11TC微涨$14至$20,020，Handysize 7TC升$118至$15,508，结构性分化明显。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: Capesize太平洋航线C5跌破$14.50，情绪转弱但$14.00附近获支撑；Panamax大西洋稳住而太平洋续跌；Supramax亚洲端出现询盘回暖，FFA买盘支撑Q3/Q4合约；Handysize亚洲航线连创新高，太平洋租金$17,300+。FFA远月曲线趋平，Cape Cal27跌至$26,400，Pmax Cal27在$15,500企稳。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: Capesize C3/C5跨区套利机会需关注巴西及西非发货人动态；Supramax亚洲短途S5（西非-北中国$24,529）领涨值得关注；Handysize太平洋航线HS6/HS7突破$17,300，Jul+Aug strip在$18,400-18,800区间活跃。

Supramax亚洲端需求回暖能否持续需观察后续到港货量

route_focus.view: 巴西-中国航线C3报$36.632（-0.218），大西洋端询盘微增但买方出价$36.50，卖方要价$37.00-37.50，价差抑制成交，情绪略软。
泛太航线5TC租金$20,285（-322），亚洲端续跌但大西洋稳住；FFA Jun 26报$20,750-20,850，Q3 26报$20,600-20,700，曲线后半段支撑较强。
Skaw-Passero至Rio航线报$6,854（+8），欧洲-南美往返需求平稳；对比HS4美湾航线$18,257（+178），美湾发运显著活跃。
